sources.locator: Printed pp.13–16; Exercise 2.1.3 p.19; Definition 2.13 and Proposition 2.14 pp.23–25; Proposition 2.15 pp.25–26; Propositions 2.16–2.17 pp.26–27; §2.4 opening pp.28–29; §2.7 pp.49–53 through Exercise 2.7.11. PDF page index = printed page +13.

contents.name: Definition 2.1
contents.support: Inverse-image preservation; source probability setting is expanded definitionally to general measures.

contents.name: Definition 2.1 invertibility clause and footnote
contents.support: Bimeasurable inverse on an invariant conull restriction; actual and mod-null invertibility separated.

contents.name: Generating-family paragraph following Definition 2.1
contents.support: Exact increasing finite-measure pi-system exhaustion supplied by the earlier local uniqueness theorem.

contents.name: Example 2.2
contents.reason: Circle rotation construction and preservation belong to the recurrence examples development.

contents.name: Example 2.3
contents.reason: Compact-group rotations require the Haar-measure development and are not part of this abstract systems pair.

contents.name: Example 2.4
contents.reason: The explicit circle doubling map is assigned to the recurrence pair, not this common-language supplier.

contents.name: Example 2.5
contents.reason: Surjective compact-group endomorphisms use Haar uniqueness beyond this pair’s prescribed measure-space scope.

contents.name: Lemma 2.6
contents.support: Indicator/simple/monotone proof extended to arbitrary nonnegative functions and complex integrable components.

contents.name: Definition 2.7
contents.support: Conull measurable restrictions support the mod-null convention; general factor theory is not used.

contents.name: Exercise 2.1.3
contents.support: Inverse-image Boolean identities; completion additionally uses the earlier local completion theorem.

contents.name: Definition 2.13
contents.support: Ergodicity is relative to the invariant measure; null/conull formulation handles general measure spaces.

contents.name: Proposition 2.14(1)–(2), limsup construction
contents.support: The measurable limsup is strictly invariant and agrees modulo a measurable null set; no completeness needed.

contents.name: Proposition 2.14(3)–(4)
contents.support: Sweep-out uses finiteness to turn containment and equal measure into mod-null invariance.

contents.name: Proposition 2.14(5)
contents.support: Countable level fibers prove constancy; real and imaginary parts give complex statement.

contents.name: §2.4 Associated Unitary Operators, opening isometry argument
contents.support: Pullback isometry and invertible inverse; Lp extension proved by integral invariance and superlevel sets.

contents.name: Lemma 2.18
contents.support: Invariant L2 functions are constants: absorbed without introducing spectral or abstract Hilbert machinery.

contents.name: §2.4 adjoint and projection discussion, equations (2.5)–(2.7)
contents.reason: Abstract adjoints and orthogonal projections are not needed to prove pullback norm preservation; the page expressly stops before spectral machinery.

contents.name: §2.7 preliminary Cesaro ergodicity characterization (2.30)–(2.31)
contents.reason: The non-absolute mean criterion requires the mean ergodic theorem; it is not the weak-mixing definition used here.

contents.name: Definition 2.32
contents.support: Set correlations define strong mixing on probability spaces.

contents.name: Example 2.33
contents.reason: The circle-rotation nonmixing witness is assigned to recurrence, which owns the circle model.

contents.name: Definition 2.34
contents.reason: Mixing of higher orders is a separate stronger property not asserted by the implication chain in this pair.

contents.name: Definition 2.35 and following Cesaro observation
contents.support: Absolute values stay inside the Cesaro mean; the elementary implication is proved in the chain theorem.

contents.name: Theorem 2.36
contents.reason: Spectral and product criteria require the next pair’s local Hilbert and kernel machinery; no such equivalence is used here.

contents.name: Corollaries 2.37–2.39
contents.reason: Product and iterate weak-mixing consequences depend on the spectral/product criterion beyond this supplier’s boundary.

contents.name: Example 2.40
contents.reason: Irrational-rotation failure of weak mixing uses the circle model owned by the recurrence pair.

contents.name: Exercises 2.7.1–2.7.2
contents.reason: Uniform or eventual exact independence forces triviality; those strengthened hypotheses are not used by either mixing criterion.

contents.name: Exercise 2.7.3(1)–(2)
contents.support: Source uses a generating semi-algebra; local finite inclusion-exclusion first extends a generating pi-system containing X to its Boolean algebra.

contents.name: Exercise 2.7.3(3)
contents.reason: The non-absolute Cesaro ergodicity characterization belongs with mean ergodic theory, unlike the two mixing tests included here.

contents.name: Exercise 2.7.4
contents.reason: Triviality only of invariant generator members is not the full ergodicity test; no such claim is made in this page.

contents.name: Exercise 2.7.5
contents.support: Strong mixing extends by uniform L2 approximation; dense-set version is an immediate same-proof observation.

contents.name: Exercise 2.7.6
contents.reason: Compact abelian automorphism mixing uses Fourier/spectral machinery expressly outside the abstract supplier pair.

contents.name: Exercise 2.7.7
contents.support: Weak-mixing complex correlations and absolute Cesaro mean; prove by finite simple expansion and uniform L2 error.

contents.name: Exercise 2.7.8
contents.reason: Testing only identical functions is an additional polarization criterion; the design specifies the two-function formulation.

contents.name: Exercise 2.7.9
contents.reason: Bernoulli mixing of every order goes beyond the assigned abstract implication and density criteria.

contents.name: Exercise 2.7.10
contents.reason: The Renyi same-set criterion is a distinct reduction not needed for a generating-pi-system test or the two-function reformulation.

contents.name: Exercise 2.7.11
contents.reason: The simultaneous positive-intersection characterization is beyond the implication chain and involves further weak-mixing equivalences.

contents.name: Proposition 2.15 cylinder approximation argument
contents.support: Finite-measure approximation by a generating algebra is generalized locally by the sigma-algebra-of-approximable-sets proof; the Bernoulli construction is not imported.

contents.name: Proposition 2.15 Bernoulli shift ergodicity
contents.reason: Product probability spaces and Bernoulli shifts are beyond the assigned finite-system examples; only the approximation argument is harvested.

contents.name: Propositions 2.16–2.17 rotations and doubling-map ergodicity
contents.reason: Concrete circle transformations belong to the recurrence application pair; this supplier retains abstract ergodicity criteria.

canonical.name: Compositions, iterates and completions preserve invariance
canonical.locator: Local proof plan with references in items ledger

canonical.name: Integral invariance under measure-preserving maps
canonical.locator: Local proof plan with references in items ledger
canonical.support: Indicators, finite nonnegative simple functions, monotone convergence, then positive/negative and real/imaginary parts.

canonical.name: The Koopman operator
canonical.locator: Local proof plan with references in items ledger
canonical.support: Pullbacks of null measurable sets are null; therefore the expression is independent of representatives.

canonical.name: Koopman operators are linear isometries
canonical.locator: Local proof plan with references in items ledger
canonical.support: For finite p use ∫|f∘T|^p=∫|f|^p; at infinity compare all superlevel null sets in both directions. Inverse composition provides surjectivity when applicable. Real quotient facts apply to real functions and moduli only; the complex quotient theorem supplies complex linear operations. For invertibility modulo null sets use the measurable inverse on the invariant conull restriction and zero extension; its inverse preserves restricted measure by applying preservation to T(E). canonical.name: Strict and mod-null invariant sigma-algebras
canonical.locator: Local proof plan with references in items ledger
canonical.support: Both families contain only measurable sets. Do not assert they always differ: identity makes them equal.

canonical.name: Both invariant families are sigma-algebras
canonical.locator: Local proof plan with references in items ledger
canonical.support: Complement commutes with pullback; symmetric difference for a countable union is contained in the union of component symmetric differences.

canonical.name: Mod-null invariant sets have strict representatives
canonical.locator: Local proof plan with references in items ledger
canonical.support: Each E Δ T^-n E is null by telescoping; the countable union contains E Δ F. Dropping the first term of a limsup proves exact invariance. No completeness needed.

canonical.name: Ergodicity relative to an invariant measure
canonical.locator: Local proof plan with references in items ledger
canonical.support: Name the measure. Permit general measures in the definition, but state subsequent probability hypotheses explicitly.

canonical.name: Equivalent invariant-set and invariant-function criteria for ergodicity
canonical.locator: Local proof plan with references in items ledger
canonical.support: The limsup representative lemma equates strict and mod-null set criteria. For a.e.-invariant real f every rational level set is invariant modulo null sets. Equivalently partition R into dyadic half-open intervals of length 2^-n: exactly one fiber has measure one for each n; their countable intersection is conull and f has a single finite value there. Apply to both components for complex f. Indicators establish all converse directions. Only measurable exceptional sets are removed, so completeness is unnecessary.

canonical.name: Positive sets sweep out ergodic probability systems
canonical.locator: Local proof plan with references in items ledger
canonical.support: The union pulls back into itself with equal finite measure, so is mod-null invariant. Use countable subadditivity and the complement of an invariant set for the converses.

canonical.name: Strong and weak mixing on a probability space
canonical.locator: Local proof plan with references in items ledger
canonical.support: Absolute values occur inside the Cesaro sum. These definitions use probability normalization.

canonical.name: Mixing implies weak mixing, which implies ergodicity
canonical.locator: Local proof plan with references in items ledger
canonical.support: Split Cesaro averages into a finite initial segment and small tail; apply weak mixing to a strict invariant set against itself.

canonical.name: Approximation in symmetric difference by a generating algebra
canonical.locator: Local proof plan with references in items ledger
canonical.support: Let D be the sets approximable in symmetric difference by the generating algebra C. D contains C; complements preserve errors. For E=union E_j with E_j in D and ε>0, continuity from below and μ(X)<∞ give m with μ(E\union_{j≤m}E_j)<ε/2; choose finitely many algebra approximants with total error <ε/2. Thus D is a sigma-algebra and minimality gives D=A. Choices are finite for each tolerance.

canonical.name: Mixing is checkable on a generating pi-system
canonical.locator: Local proof plan with references in items ledger
canonical.support: Extend to the algebra of its finite Boolean combinations by finite inclusion-exclusion, then approximate both sets. The error is bounded uniformly in n by twice the sum of their symmetric-difference errors.

canonical.name: Mixing correlations extend to L2 functions
canonical.locator: Local proof plan with references in items ledger
canonical.support: For indicators this is precisely the set correlation with the two sets interchanged. For finite complex simple sums expand and use the triangle inequality, also inside the Cesaro average. Given ε>0 choose simple a,b with L2 errors <ε using the finite-simple clause of complex density (no smooth-density clause or countable selection). Koopman isometry and complex Cauchy–Schwarz give |C_n(f,g)-C_n(a,b)|≤2(||f-a||2||g||2+||a||2||g-b||2) uniformly in n, since ||1||2=1. This tends to zero with ε. The old real Cauchy–Schwarz edge is used only on the real moduli in the same integral estimate; no equality clause or finite-dimensional projection is used.

canonical.name: A preserving permutation on two equal atoms
canonical.locator: Local proof plan with references in items ledger
canonical.support: Check the empty, singleton and full sets by inverse images. Countable additivity is finite additivity here because a disjoint family has at most two nonempty members.

canonical.name: A preserving identity need not be ergodic
canonical.locator: Local proof plan with references in items ledger
canonical.support: Every inverse image equals the original set; {0} is strictly invariant of measure 1/2, refuting preservation implies ergodicity.

canonical.name: The Koopman matrix for a two-point swap
canonical.locator: Local proof plan with references in items ledger
canonical.support: The finite-p norm is ((|a|^p+|b|^p)/2)^(1/p), and the infinity norm is max(|a|,|b|). Both are unchanged by swapping. Establish the underlying preservation directly on the four sets before invoking the theorem.

canonical.name: Finite simple analytic families and their exact endpoint norms
canonical.locator: Local proof plan with references in items ledger
canonical.support: For a nonzero coefficient a use phase(a)=a/|a| and exp(p((1−z)/p0+z/p1)log|a|); define zero coefficients identically zero, never log 0 or 0^0. For finite r use the analogous b formula with r((1−z)/r0+z/r1). For r=∞ use constant g. At θ the exponent equals one. On vertical boundaries moduli are fixed powers, yielding the norm identities by finite sums, or the essential maximum for ri=∞. Discard null fibers for nonzero norm claims. Holomorphicity is coefficientwise via the entire exponential and affine composition; no Banach-valued holomorphic theorem is needed.

canonical.name: Riesz–Thorin estimate on the finite simple core
canonical.locator: Local proof plan with references in items ledger
canonical.support: Normalize nonzero f and finite simple dual test g to norms one. Use a1, including the constant g family when qθ=1. H(z)=∫(Tf_z)g_z is a finite sum of entire coefficient products times fixed integrals ∫T1_Ej 1_Fk. Those integrals are finite by endpoint Holder and finite-measure test support. This also proves boundedness on the whole closed strip and boundary continuity; no exchanging infinite integrals and derivatives. Endpoint estimates give |H(it)|≤M0 and |H(1+it)|≤M1. Apply exactly thm-hadamard-three-lines, including a zero Mi, then the membership version of the dual-test lemma. Homogeneity recovers arbitrary f; zero f follows from linearity. For arbitrary spaces with finite qi: choose representatives h_j=T1_Ej and set Y0=union_{j,n}{|h_j|>1/n}. Each level set has finite measure since n^(-qi)ν{|h_j|>1/n}≤∫|h_j|^qi.
